name: וקטור בין שתי נקודות בהצגת i, j, k (באנגלית)

functions.name: texp
functions.body: if numberp(x) and x<0 then concat("\\left(",tex1(x),"\\right)") else tex1(x)

functions.name: texsumf
functions.body: block([L:first(args(e))], concat(tex1(first(L)), apply(sconcat, map(lambda([t], concat("+",texp(t))), rest(L)))))

functions.name: texnsum
functions.body: block([L:first(args(e))], concat(tex1(first(L)), apply(sconcat, map(lambda([t], if numberp(t) and t<0 then concat("-",tex1(-t)) else concat("+",tex1(t))), rest(L)))))

questiontext:
Given that \(A\) is the point \(({{CT:0}},\,{{CT:1}},\,{{CT:2}})\) and that \(B\) is the point \(({{CT:3}},\,{{CT:4}},\,{{CT:5}})\)

then the vector \(\mathbf{r}\) from \(A\) to \(B\) is

[[input:ans1]] \(\mathbf{i}\) \(+\) [[input:ans2]] \(\mathbf{j}\) \(+\) [[input:ans3]] \(\mathbf{k}\).
[[validation:ans1]] [[validation:ans2]] [[validation:ans3]]
generalfeedback:
Outline: The vector from \(A\) to \(B\) is the position vector of the end point minus that of the start point: \(\mathbf{r}=\overrightarrow{AB}=B-A\). Subtract the coordinates one by one.
Step 1 — The two points
The given points are

\[ A=({{CT:0}},\,{{CT:1}},\,{{CT:2}}),\qquad B=({{CT:3}},\,{{CT:4}},\,{{CT:5}}). \]

Step 2 — Subtracting the coordinates
Each component of \(\mathbf{r}\) is the coordinate of \(B\) minus the same coordinate of \(A\) (the order matters: \(A-B\) is the vector from \(B\) to \(A\)):

\[ \begin{aligned} \mathbf{r} &= B-A = ({{CT:3}},\,{{CT:4}},\,{{CT:5}})-({{CT:0}},\,{{CT:1}},\,{{CT:2}}) \\ &= \left({{CT:6}}\right)\mathbf{i}+\left({{CT:7}}\right)\mathbf{j}+\left({{CT:8}}\right)\mathbf{k} \\ &= {{CT:9}}\,\mathbf{i} + {{CT:10}}\,\mathbf{j} + {{CT:11}}\,\mathbf{k}. \end{aligned} \]

on_true.feedback:
This is the vector from B to A. Each component is the additive inverse of that in the vector from A to B.

Your answer is

\[\left({{CT:0}} - {{CT:3}}\right)\mathbf{i} + \left({{CT:1}} - {{CT:4}}\right)\mathbf{j} + \left({{CT:2}} - {{CT:5}}\right)\mathbf{k}\mbox{.}\]

The vector from A to B is

\[ \mathbf{r} = \left({{CT:3}} - {{CT:0}}\right)\mathbf{i} + \left({{CT:4}} - {{CT:1}}\right) \mathbf{j} + \left({{CT:5}} - {{CT:2}}\right)\mathbf{k}\mbox{.}\]

Your answer is

\[\left({{CT:0}} + {{CT:3}}\right)\mathbf{i} + \left({{CT:1}} + {{CT:4}}\right)\mathbf{j} + \left({{CT:2}} + {{CT:5}}\right)\mathbf{k}\mbox{.}\]

The vector from A to B is

\[ \mathbf{r} = \left({{CT:3}} - {{CT:0}}\right)\mathbf{i} + \left({{CT:4}} - {{CT:1}}\right) \mathbf{j} + \left({{CT:5}} - {{CT:2}}\right)\mathbf{k}\mbox{.}\]
Your answer is the vector from the origin to the midpoint between A and B. You may have used the wrong method.
